newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Prairie harvest 25 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Canada Prairie harvest 25 percent complete.

text.p: Canada's Prairie harvest was at least 25 percent complete by Thursday with 10 to 20 percent of crops still maturing and at risk of frost damage, a Canadian Wheat Board weather and crop analyst said.

"We had 20 percent harvested at the start of the week but it hasn't progressed much since. It's at 25 to 30 percent today because of the cool and wet weather," Paul Bullock, CWB director of weather and crop surveillance, told Reuters.
The jet stream dropped to southern Alberta, central Saskatchewan and Manitoba, bringing storm systems that track along that line since Sunday, Bullock said.
Environment Canada issued severe thunderstorm watches for most of the eastern Prairie grain belt at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT.
The federal meteorological agency forecast a likelihood of frost for the southwest Prairie grainbelt Friday morning due to clear skies and cool daytime temperatures.
The CWB's Bullock said he would not be surprised if that region saw a frost Friday morning, but most crops were already combined there.
"I'm more concerned right now about the wet conditions. At this point we'll see a bit of loss on quality. We need 10 days of relatively dry weather to come off okay," Bullock said.
"Unfortunately it'll take two to three days to dry down," he said.
